macro_blurb: Today's session is shaped primarily by easing Middle East risk premia, with President Trump stating that a framework deal with Iran covering the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is "largely negotiated" and pending announcement — a development relevant for energy-sensitive sectors and broader risk appetite on both sides of the Atlantic. That backdrop helped extend last week's rally that pushed the S&P 500 back near record highs. In Europe, political risk is more idiosyncratic: tens of thousands protested in Belgrade demanding the ouster of Serbia's president, while in Germany an intensifying SPD debate over the "Brandmauer" toward the AfD adds noise to the domestic political setup. Ukraine's renewed focus on its recruitment shortfall in the war's fifth year remains a slower-burning overlay for EU defense and fiscal narratives.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a US deep-value print, full stop. All 10 picks are US-listed despite 992 names screened, with an average Value percentile of 84.9 and Momentum of 85.4 — the rare combination where cheap is also working. Financial Services dominates at 3 of 10 (EG, ALL, CINF), Healthcare adds 2 (CNC, DVA), and the composite range is tight (73.8–82.4), so there is no runaway favorite. Quality, at 60.6 average, is the soft component — the screen is paying for cheapness and tape, not for franchise.

The clearest thread runs through insurance: Everest (EG), Allstate (ALL) and Cincinnati Financial (CINF) all surface on Value + Quality, with trailing P/Es of 7.2x, 4.8x and 9.6x against a 17.5x sector median and FCF yields of 28.6%, 22.3% and 10.6%. The market is pricing reserve and catastrophe doubt across the book. A second thread is cheap-and-running US cyclicals — CF, APA and DAL all post 100th-, 100th- and 95th-percentile Value with 3-month returns of 28%, 35% and 14%; the easing Hormuz risk premium cuts directly against APA's setup even as it lifts DAL's fuel math.

The outlier is MO — defensive, no Quality score, carried by a 5.74% yield and rare positive momentum in Consumer Defensive. Conspicuous by absence: Technology, Utilities and Real Estate, zero picks between them out of 186 scored — a screen this value-tilted is structurally short duration and growth. Watch the Iran framework announcement (re-rates APA immediately) and Best Buy's May 28 print (tests whether the cheap-cyclical thesis survives a real comp).
